threatModel.summary: Scope 4B1 adds a standalone, local, bounded STATIC CUDA incidence-motif executable and developer qualification transport/harness. The transport canonicalizes a Hypergraph-family incidence object, packs dense H2V rows and identity/version/device metadata, and the executable accepts only --request <local-file>. Native code reads and parses that bounded regular file, derives the classification table on the host, counts triples exclusively in a CUDA kernel, and returns JSON; the harness checks binding and structure and compares counts to an external CPU oracle. Production capability declarations remain SSSP-only. Evidence: candy-runtime/test/hypergraph-motif-cuda-contract.mjs:8; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:53; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:155; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:186; candy-runtime/test/run-hypergraph-motif-cuda-qualification.mjs:49; candy-runtime/src/capabilities/capabilityRegistry.js:48.
trustBoundaries: External incidence data -> qualified JS adapter: exact object keys exclude H2H/V2H/projection additions, semantic IDs are type tagged and deduplicated, memberships must reference declared vertices and be unique, and rows are deterministically sorted. The transport supplies stricter edge/incidence overrides and a work limit. Evidence: src/candy/adapters/hypergraphIncidenceAdapter.js:34; src/candy/adapters/hypergraphIncidenceAdapter.js:75; src/candy/adapters/hypergraphIncidenceAdapter.js:120; src/candy/adapters/identifierMapping.js:3; candy-runtime/test/hypergraph-motif-cuda-contract.mjs:12.

Local CLI caller -> native file reader: exactly argc=3 with argv[1]=--request is accepted. The chosen argv[2] is an authorized local read path, using ordinary OS resolution for relative paths and parent-directory symlinks. O_NOFOLLOW rejects the final symlink, O_NONBLOCK prevents FIFO blocking, fstat requires a regular file, and the same descriptor carries both initial size checking and bounded reading. Evidence: candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:53; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:267; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/README.md:22. Local-path authorization and parent-symlink semantics are also supplied user context.

Request text -> native arrays/CUDA inputs: strict token ordering, unsigned decimal parsing with field-specific bounds, STATIC and Hypergraph-family restrictions, lowercase UTF-16 identity encoding, strict offsets, sorted unique memberships, vertex-range checks, and final END/no trailing content establish the dense incidence contract. Evidence: candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:70; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:96.

Native host -> CUDA device: device existence, requested device selection, grid/block limits, checked allocation arithmetic, bounded validated incidence buffers and host-derived lookup precede launch. Counting occurs in count_triples with i<j<k, merging three sorted rows and unsigned 64-bit atomic increments; host work derives classification and validates returned count bounds rather than enumerating counts. Evidence: candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:155; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:168; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:186; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:205.

Qualification harness -> local child process: Linux directly invokes the repository-derived binary with argv [--request, derived-request-path]; Windows invokes wsl.exe with [-d, Ubuntu, --exec, command, ...args] and drive paths mapped to /mnt/<drive>/. Sanitizer selection is allowlisted and uses /usr/local/cuda-13.4/bin/compute-sanitizer. Commands are invoked without shell mode, with 60-second timeout and 8 MiB output buffer; the environment is inherited except the dedicated no-visible-device test. Request contents cannot select an executable or output path. Evidence: candy-runtime/test/run-hypergraph-motif-cuda-qualification.mjs:12; candy-runtime/test/run-hypergraph-motif-cuda-qualification.mjs:30.

Native JSON -> qualification result consumer: exact keys, schema, algorithm, taxonomy, backend, STATIC mode, graph identity/version, device index, 30 safe nonnegative counts, count sum/combinatorial bound, execution flags and metadata formats are checked before every bin and total are compared to the CPU oracle. Evidence: candy-runtime/test/hypergraph-motif-cuda-contract.mjs:42; candy-runtime/test/run-hypergraph-motif-cuda-qualification.mjs:49.

Developer build -> standalone binaries: CUDA_ARCH is mandatory; NVCC/NVFLAGS are trusted local build configuration, and fault macros produce separate suffix-named binaries rather than runtime request switches. Success checks explicit cleanup before result emission; failure destructors perform best-effort cleanup. Evidence: candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/Makefile:1; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/Makefile:18; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:175; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:206; candy-runtime/native/hypergraph-motif-cuda/src/main.cu:252.

Qualification evidence -> runtime capability authority: the harness writes fixed JSON artifact names; build and temporary request directories are ignored. Existing capability declaration code only registers qualified OpenMP and CUDA SSSP capabilities, with no motif registration.
